title: NASA HRP — exercise countermeasures and gravity environments
description: NASA describes 2.5 hours of scheduled daily ISS exercise using ARED, a treadmill, and a cycle ergometer. Our catalog represents microgravity (0g), Moon (0.16g), and Mars (0.38g) as approximate environment profiles. Exercise loads and form thresholds are team-defined prototype settings, not NASA prescriptions.

links.label: NASA astronaut health and daily exercise

title: NASA OSDR and LSDA — life-sciences research references
description: OSDR and the Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA) provide research context for the implemented 30-day Earth-Baseline Strength Retention and Flight Surgeon telemetry. The retention equation and telemetry schema are team-defined; NASA participant records are not imported or used to validate them. LSDA is accessed through the NASA Life Sciences Portal.

title: NASA MGS MOLA / Planetary Data System — Mars geography
description: The catalog uses a 4,000 km Valles Marineris expedition and a 600 km Olympus Mons expedition. NASA describes these as approximate canyon length and volcano diameter, respectively. The Olympus expedition is a game distance, not a measured ascent. MGS MOLA is the official topographic archive; terrain rasters are not imported into this prototype.

links.label: NASA PDS MGS MOLA topography archive

title: CSA — TBone and MARROW
description: TBone studies bone loss and recovery; MARROW studies bone marrow and blood-cell changes. These Canadian Space Agency studies provide scientific context for musculoskeletal monitoring. Their participant data are not imported into the exercise engine.

title: ESA — communication delays and autonomous health monitoring
description: ESA's Mars500 study used a 20-minute communication delay, while EchoFinder-2 illustrates autonomous health assessment for distant missions. Our 24-minute blackout is a team-selected resilience scenario, rather than an ESA medical protocol.

title: JAXA — Kibo muscle-atrophy countermeasure research
description: Kibo's Zebrafish Muscle 2 research investigates microgravity-related muscle atrophy and potential countermeasures. This is a scientific reference; the project's exercise thresholds are not derived from this animal study.
